evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode="batched" with aggregation="weighted_mean" (functional/judge.toml:3,21; polish/judge.toml:3,15; visual/judge.toml:3,15); both gates are batched all_pass (gates/render/judge.toml:15, gates/constraints/judge.toml:15) and are exempt. Each scored prompt carries explicit independence-and-continue wording: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature'; polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.'; visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.' Shared per-feature failure handling (functional/polish/visual prompt.md:7) says 'give that criterion its lowest score ... state what you observed, and move on', and each prompt ends with 'Preserve every completed independent observation' (functional:53, polish:18, visual:16). Grep of scored prompts, scored judge.toml descriptions and app_context.md for stop/halt/first-failure/skip-the-rest wording found none (the only 'abort' hits are polish's instruction to abort one send request, unrelated). The template's 'Fail fast ... stop' bullet is absent; nothing tells the judge to stop at first failure. The only all-criteria zeroing is the in-dimension global browser gate (blank/static shell or failed shared-storage check), which the staged contract/check-rubric-prompt.py requires scored prompts to restate, so it is the expected gate, not a cascade from one criterion's miss. Counterexample probes: (a) a weak app that fails reorder in protocol M cannot zero later rows because the prompt orders continuation and re-setup on a new job; (b) a conforming app is not zeroed by one failure since there is no stop instruction. Observation for other rows' owners (not a row-38 wording defect): polish hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread (polish/judge.toml:23,32) state 'this row is 0' if the live update/message does not arrive within 15 s, so an app without live push also loses functional hro_live_board/hro_msg_exchange; that is a precondition dependency/double-deduction question for checks 26/28/40, not prompt wording that stops scoring. Run verdict: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope says full configured grading is absent), so actual judge compliance with the wording is not measured; this row's verify procedure is a source wording check, which is fully satisfied.
